x.ASV: A Psalm of the sons of Korah; a Song. His foundation is in the holy mountains.
x.Darby: Of the sons of Korah. A Psalm. A Song. His foundation is in the mountains of holiness.
x.KJV: A Psalm or Song for the sons of Korah. His foundation is in the holy mountains.
x.YLT: By sons of Korah. --A Psalm, a song. His foundation is in holy mountains.

nt: The word **sons** refers to the descendants of Korah. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Of those who are descended from Korah]
The pronoun **His** refers to Yahweh, who is named in the next verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh’s foundation]

Without naming it, the psalmist is speaking of the city of Zion as if it were a building that has a **foundation**. This represents the idea that God has firmly established the city. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The city he has established is on the mountains of holiness]

The psalmist is using the possessive form to describe **mountains** that are characterized by **holiness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [mountains that are holy]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [is on the mountains that are holy]

x.ASV: Jehovah loveth the gates of Zion More than all the dwellings of Jacob.
x.Darby: Jehovah loveth the gates of Zion more than all the habitations of Jacob.
x.KJV: The Lord loveth the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
x.YLT: Jehovah is loving the gates of Zion Above all the tabernacles of Jacob.

nt: The psalmist is using **the gates of Zion** to represent the entire city of Zion. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Zion itself]

Here, **the dwellings of Jacob** represents the places where the descendants of Jacob live. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the places where the descendants of Jacob live]

x.ASV: Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God. [Selah
x.Darby: Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city ofGod. Selah.
x.KJV: Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God. Selah.
x.YLT: Honourable things are spoken in Thee, O city of God. Selah.

nt: The expression **Glorious things are spoken of you** uses a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [God declares glorious things about you]

The psalmist is speaking to the city of Zion as if it could hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about how honored Zion is. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if the psalmist were speaking to people about Zion. Alternate translation: [spoken about Zion, the city of God]
The psalmist is using this possessive form to mean that Zion is the city where God dwells. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [city where God dwells]

x.ASV: I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon as among them that know me: Behold, Philistia, and Tyre, with Ethiopia: This one was born there.
x.Darby: I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon among them that know me; behold Philistia, and Tyre, with Ethiopia: this [man] was born there.
x.KJV: I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon to them that know me: behold Philistia, and Tyre, with Ethiopia; this man was born there.
x.YLT: I mention Rahab and Babel to those knowing Me, Lo, Philistia, and Tyre, with Cush! This one was born there.

nt: The pronoun **I** refers to Yahweh, who is the speaker from this point in the psalm. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh, will mention]

Here the psalmist is speaking of Egypt as if it were the sea monster **Rahab**. The psalmist may be comparing Egypt to Rahab because of the way God rescued Israel from Israel at the Sea of Reeds. It is not referring to the person named Rahab mentioned elsewhere in the Bible. You could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Egypt]

In the phrase **the ones knowing me**, the pronoun **me** refers to Yahweh, who is the speaker. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the ones knowing me, Yahweh]

Yahweh is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [take note]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [I will also mention Philistia and Tyre with Cush]

This is a quotation that Yahweh says about each person from the nations he has listed. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could indicate this with a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.

The expression **was born** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [began life]

x.ASV: Yea, of Zion it shall be said, This one and that one was born in her; And the Most High himself will establish her.
x.Darby: And of Zion it shall be said, This one and that one was born in her; and the Most High himself shall establish her.
x.KJV: And of Zion it shall be said, This and that man was born in her: and the highest himself shall establish her.
x.YLT: And of Zion it is said: Each one was born in her, And He, the Most High, doth establish her.

nt: The expression **it will be said** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [everyone will declare]

The psalmist is using **Man and man** as a common expression of the culture to mean “each and every person.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Each person was born in her] or [Person after person was born in her]
This is a direct quotation of what people will say about Zion. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could indicate this with a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.

The expression **was born** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [began life]

The pronoun **he** refers to God Most High. The psalmist repeats the pronoun **he** for emphasis before naming **the Most High** directly. He is emphasizing that it is only God who can do this. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [God Most High himself will establish her]

x.ASV: Jehovah will count, when he writeth up the peoples, This one was born there. [Selah
x.Darby: Jehovah will count, when he inscribeth the peoples, This [man] was born there. Selah.
x.KJV: The Lord shall count, when he writeth up the people, that this man was born there. Selah.
x.YLT: Jehovah doth recount in the describing of the peoples, `This one was born there.' Selah.

nt: The psalmist is using this possessive form to mean a record that documents the peoples. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the record that lists the peoples]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **writing**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what is written about]

This is a quotation that Yahweh will record about each person from the nations. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could indicate this with a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.

The expression **was born** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [began life]

x.ASV: They that sing as well as they that dance shall say, All my fountains are in thee.
x.Darby: As well the singers as the dancers [shall say], All my springs are in thee.
x.KJV: As well the singers as the players on instruments shall be there: all my springs are in thee.
x.YLT: Singers also as players on instruments, All my fountains are in Thee!

nt: The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And the singers, like the pipers, will declare]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the pipers** play music, so **the singers** also make music. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [together with the pipers]

The singers are speaking of Zion as if it were a place from which **springs** of water flow. This represents the idea that Zion is the source of all life and blessing. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [All that sustains our lives comes from you]

This is a direct quotation of what the singers and pipers will say. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could indicate this with a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.
